title: Tideway launch minute slate and observability lane - July 2027 (draft)
content:
Context: codename = \"Tideway\". This is a compact, minute-by-minute slate for the July 2027 weekday launch window. Focus: low-latency routing change + small model variant swap (v2 -> v2-quant). Goal: validate throughput at typical 25% traffic, then ramp to 50% and hold before full flip. Keep it conservative — we prefer slow roll + clear telemetry gates.

Objectives:
- Safety-first canary: validate latency P95 and error-rate at 25% of baseline traffic for 30m before ramp.
- Telemetry anchors in place: latency, token-cost per request, KV-cache hit rate, tail-SLOs.
- Fast fallback path: automated traffic drain + pinned older variant fallback.

Preflight (48–2 hours before):
- [ ] Confirm JIRA RINF-3124 all sub-tasks closed or flagged for post-launch.
- [ ] Smoke tests green on staging (smoke-suite/staging #tideway).
- [ ] Observability dashboards ready: tideway-canary, tideway-telemetry-quick.
- [ ] Operator runbook pinned to Slack channel #release-tideway.
- [ ] Oncall roster confirmed for +72h (Maya, Liam, SRE rotation).
- [ ] Backfill capacity reserved (dedicated pool reservation id 77-08).

Launch day timeline (all times UTC):
T-60m: final go/no-go check-in (15m) — product, infra, SRE. Call: Zoom link pinned in Slack.
T-45m: deploy artifacts staged in canary cluster (namespace: tideway-canary). Notify #release-tideway.
T-30m: start synthetic load shows (10m). Baseline compared to previous 24h medians.
T-15m: flip config to route 5% (smoke) and run quick validation (5m).
T-00m (canary start): move to 25% traffic. Begin 30m hold. Run full telemetry checks.
T+30m: if gates pass, ramp to 50% for 20m.
T+50m: if gates pass, ramp to 100% over 10m with stepwise increases (65% -> 80% -> 100%).
T+60m+: post-ramp monitoring and gradual policy cleanup.

Rollout phases and operator actions:
- Phase A (smoke): route 5% to v2-quant, verify request/response validation. Operator: \"rlctl set-routing tideway v2-quant --percent 5\".
- Phase B (canary): \"rlctl set-routing tideway v2-quant --percent 25\". Hold 30m. Collect telemetry.
- Phase C (mid-ramp): \"rlctl set-routing tideway v2-quant --percent 50\". Hold 20m.
- Phase D (final): step increases: 65, 80, 100. Monitor for rollback triggers.

Primary telemetry checks (must pass to proceed):
- Latency P95 (tail): must be <= baseline P95 + 18% for canary. Query (PromQL):
  - max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))[30m:5m])
- Error rate (5xx) < 0.5% of requests during hold window. Query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\",route=\"tideway\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=\"tideway\"}[5m])) < 0.005
- KV-cache hit rate > 70% (otherwise costs will climb). Query: rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]) > 0.7
- Token cost per 1k requests should not exceed 1.25x baseline. Pull from cost-metrics service metric: model_token_cost_per_request{model=\"v2-quant\"}
- Queue depth / backlog should remain below 20 per replica.

Alerting thresholds (immediate rollback if hit):
- sustained error-rate > 1% for 5m -> auto-drain to 0% and fallback to v2.
- P95 latency breach > baseline P95 * 1.5 for 10m -> operator review, recommend rollback.
- KV-cache hit < 50% for 15m -> pause ramp and investigate.

Rollback procedure (fast fallback):
- Run: \"rlctl route tideway v2 --force\" -> moves 100% back to stable v2.
- If automated drain configured: POST /ops/route/drain?tideway=true triggers staged 90s drain per host.
- Inform: post to #release-tideway with header \"ROLLBACK: Tideway\"; page oncall.
- Capture: collect traces and sample logs (run: ops-ci/tideway/capture-sample.sh --since 15m).

Operator cheat sheet (commands & snippets):
- Check current routing: rlctl get-routing tideway --json | jq '.routes'
- Set routing: rlctl set-routing tideway v2-quant --percent 25 --note \"canary-start\"
- Force rollback: rlctl set-routing tideway v2 --percent 100 --reason \"auto-rollback\"
- Trigger synthetic tests: curl -X POST https://ci.internal/synthetics/run?tideway=1
- Capture logs: gcloud logging read \"resource.labels.service_name=\\\"tideway\\\"\" --limit 1000 > tideway-logs-sample.ndjson

Communication protocol:
- Primary channel: #release-tideway (public watch).
- Incident channel: #ops-urgent (page if rollback).
- Standby Zoom: (link in pinned doc).
- Status updates cadence: every 10m during canary, every 5m during mid-ramp, immediate on failures.

Post-launch checklist (first 24h):
- [ ] Confirm 72h retention for canary traces captured.
- [ ] Annotate release notes page with observed regressions and follow-ups.
- [ ] Bookblame: tag owners on any test flake or perf regression jobs.
- [ ] Run cost snapshot and compare token spend delta vs baseline.
- [ ] Schedule retrospective within 3 business days.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Are there any downstream jobs that expect older model logits shape? Quick grep in monorepo for \"logits_v1\" gave two hits (solutions/search-service). Notify owners.
- Double-check that dedicated pool autoscaler has the capacity headroom for 2x normal burst. (Liam to confirm).
- Consider a temporary prefix cache warmup job before traffic ramp if KV-hit is borderline.

Quick launch log template (fill during run):
- T0: canary start: (passed/gated/rollback) -- notes
- T+15m: canary: P95=__, 5xx=__, KV-hit=__
- T+30m: canary decision: (ramp/halt/rollback) -- notes
- T+50m: mid-ramp: P95=__, 5xx=__, KV-hit=__
- Final flip: time, final percent steps, any anomalies

Postmortem placeholders (if needed):
- Timeline: minute-granular events, responsible owners.
- Root cause candidate list.
- Mitigation and long-term fix owners (assign within 48h).

Misc: keep this doc minimal and pinned. Avoid adding heavy runbooks here — link to canonical runbook in Confluence. This file is the minute-by-minute slate for the op crew for Tideway.

If anything is unclear during the run, call immediate 3-way: product -> infra -> SRE.

END.
